history_policy: This version hash-inherits every V13 workload, scored mode, jobs, checksum, timing boundary, engine-availability, acceptance, attribution metric, and pending-panel decision. It expands only the opt-in attribution coverage to every repository-owned workload and every supported 1/2/4/8-lane shared-realm row; any later workload, boundary, jobs, checksum, metric, or acceptance change creates another version.
change: Adds exact configuration/warmup/invocation attribution for both additional-panel workloads and for every supported family/additional-panel shared row at the frozen 1/2/4/8 lane counts. Shared invocation snapshots are captured only after every real JavaScript Thread has joined and must record exactly one worker run per lane.

tier_attribution.scope: one fresh zig-js process and context per workload, structural variant, execution mode, and lane count; all attribution remains opt-in and outside scored timing rows
tier_attribution.workload_coverage: all 18 base/variant families plus every additional panel; families with shared=false retain their exact frozen exclusion
tier_attribution.warmup: single and module rows retain their inherited boundary; shared rows retain the scored shared-mode warmup, including real Thread lifecycle warmup and the first cooperative collection/reuse cycle
tier_attribution.invocation: one inherited full-work call at the frozen jobs and lane input; shared snapshots occur after all lane Threads join, and retained RSS is sampled after the workload host checkpoint and before Context destruction
tier_attribution.equivalence: For warmup and invocation independently at each supported mode/lane count, every base/variant pair must select the same non-empty set of tree-walker, VM, baseline, optimizer, optimizer-OSR, and deoptimization paths and allocate exactly the same number of environments. Every shared invocation must record exactly one worker run per lane. Exact tier, timing, runtime, synchronization, allocation, GC-pause, process CPU, resident-memory, and worker values remain visible rather than normalized away; every Wasm workload must record an invocation-phase Wasm dispatch.
tier_attribution.timing_isolation: Attribution uses fresh opt-in processes and contexts outside every scored timing row; ordinary contexts retain a null execution-attribution pointer and therefore perform no tier-up, deoptimization, or process-resource clock queries.

recognizer_audit.prohibited: Every representative workload identifier is absent from engine source. Identifiers exist only in the owned workload, manifest, and benchmark tooling.
